summary: The base source still used integer all_reduce(MIN) for TP token-ID synchronization on every backend. The candidate avoids XCCL's reported integer MIN-to-SUM fallback by using XPU all_gather_into_tensor followed by a device-local minimum, preserving the prior minimum-token semantics; other backends retain all_reduce(MIN).

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before simulation of the reported XCCL integer MIN fallback: [42, 42] became 84, differing values [17, 5] became 22, and the zero boundary still proved the forbidden all_reduce was called. Raw output: reports/j-37f75653ce7c/raw/pytest_before.txt

Four passing cases: identical positive token IDs, disagreeing rank IDs with exact minimum preservation, zero across four ranks, and unchanged non-XPU MIN all-reduce dispatch. Raw output: reports/j-37f75653ce7c/raw/pytest_after_final.txt

On the assigned gfx950, the candidate local int64 reduction returned [42, 3, 4], matching independent Python minima for synthetic gathered rank values. Raw output: reports/j-37f75653ce7c/raw/gfx950_local_min_check.txt
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, syntax, and registered-test metadata checks passed.

remaining_limitations: No Intel XPU hardware, xccl/oneCCL backend, or XPU PyTorch build was available, so the reported collective failure and candidate workaround were not executed on the affected backend.
Only one assigned GPU was available; no genuine tensor-parallel or multi-rank GPU transport run was performed.
No model weights were needed or used. Grammar/structured decoding and a full HTTP serving path were not exercised because those would not qualify the missing XPU backend behavior.
Final XPU/xccl confirmation remains required before describing the upstream issue as fixed.
